themes_detail.label: Encampment spike in Morris Park
themes_detail.summary: Encampment complaints surged to 4 THIS WEEK, a 967% spike versus the 0.4 weekly average over the prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.21), signaling a sudden emergence of street homelessness or informal settlements in the district that requires immediate investigation of root causes and city response.
evidence: 4 encampment complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.21, severity: high)
967% increase represents most dramatic spike in dataset after park noise
Pattern is brand new — baseline was near-zero over prior 8 weeks, indicating acute change not chronic issue
reporting_angles: On-the-ground reporting: Where are encampments located? Are they in parks, on streets, or near transit? Interview affected residents and business owners.
City response: Has Parks Enforcement or NYPD been deployed? What is the timeline for clearing or support services? Contact CB11 and City Council.

themes_detail.label: Drug activity spike in district
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints jumped to 6 LAST WEEK, a 1500% spike from the 0.4 weekly baseline over 8 weeks (z-score: 8.08), representing the second-highest statistical anomaly and suggesting either deteriorating public safety conditions or increased visibility of existing activity.
evidence: 6 drug activity complaints last week vs. 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.08, severity: high)
1500% increase makes this the second-largest spike after park noise complaints
Converges with encampment spike THIS WEEK, suggesting interconnected street conditions issues
reporting_angles: NYPD deployment: Has the precinct increased narcotics enforcement? Interview police about visible dealing locations and prevention strategy.
Community safety perception: Canvass Morris Park residents and merchants about where drugs are visibly sold and whether they feel safe reporting activity.

themes_detail.label: Park noise complaints explode
themes_detail.summary: Noise - Park complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 2300% increase from the 0.1 weekly baseline (z-score: 8.69, the highest statistical anomaly), indicating either a specific event or deteriorating conditions at a particular park requiring field reporting.
evidence: 3 park noise complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 8.69, severity: high)
2300% spike is the single largest statistical deviation in entire dataset
Community board requests consistent park safety and amenity improvements — this may be manifestation of underlying conditions
reporting_angles: Identify the park: Which Morris Park / Pelham Parkway parks generated complaints? Cross-reference 311 data with Parks Dept records and visit in person.
Event or ongoing? Was this tied to a specific event (concert, gathering) or sign of persistent noise from homeless encampments or unauthorized activity?

themes_detail.label: Curb and street condition deterioration
themes_detail.summary: Curb condition complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK, a 540% spike versus the 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85), coupled with ongoing elevated street condition complaints (539 total over 90 days), suggesting infrastructure decay that aligns with long-standing CB budget requests for streetscape improvements.
evidence: 4 curb condition complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.6 weekly baseline (z-score: 4.85, severity: high)
540% spike coincides with broader street condition complaints (539 over 90 days), indicating systemic issue
Community Board has submitted repeated capital budget requests for streetscape improvements and catch basin cleaning to DEP — this spike validates persistent concerns
reporting_angles: Mapping deterioration: Document which streets have cracked curbs, damaged sidewalks, or blocked catch basins. Are there patterns (aging infrastructure vs. deferred maintenance)?
Budget accountability: Interview CB11 about how long they've requested streetscape funding and what response DOT and DEP have provided.

themes_detail.label: Vendor enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints spiked to 3 TWO WEEKS AGO, a 700% increase from the 0.4 weekly baseline (z-score: 5.42), suggesting either increased street vending activity or concentrated enforcement action that warrants understanding of underlying causes.
evidence: 3 vendor enforcement complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 5.42, severity: high)
700% spike represents significant but not unprecedented anomaly compared to encampment and drug activity spikes
May indicate either street vending boom or targeted city enforcement campaign
reporting_angles: Street vending landscape: Are unauthorized vendors proliferating? Interview legal street vendors and community about vending economy changes.
Enforcement intent: Contact DOC (Department of Consumer and Worker Protection) about whether they've ramped up enforcement in CD211 and why.
